title: Ethiopian Fresh Salad
community: All of Ethiopia — the ubiquitous fresh salad accompaniment
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Selata — a simple fresh salad of tomatoes, cucumber, onion, jalapeño, and coriander dressed with lemon and oil. The universal accompaniment to Ethiopian grilled fish and fried fish — its freshness and acidity cutting through the richness of spiced preparations.
longDesc: Ethiopian fresh salad is the clean counterpoint to the richly spiced dishes — tomatoes, cucumber, onion, jalapeño, and coriander dressed simply with lemon and a little oil. It appears alongside every grilled and fried fish dish and is the most neutral item on the Ethiopian table.
ingredients: ½ red onion — very thinly sliced
steps: Combine all diced vegetables and jalapeño.
Dress with lemon juice, olive oil, and salt.
chefTips: Let the salad rest 5 minutes — the salt draws out vegetable juices, creating the dressing.
Very fresh vegetables only — this salad lives or dies by the produce.
cookingScience: The salt in the dressing draws water from the vegetable cells through osmosis — this water dilutes the lemon juice and oil into a natural dressing that coats each vegetable piece without being heavy.
sustainabilityTips: Ethiopian highlands produce exceptional tomatoes and cucumbers.
servedWith: With all grilled and fried fish dishes
As a fresh counterpoint to rich wats
healthBenefits: Very high in vitamin C from tomatoes and lemon.
culturalNote: Ethiopian selata is the table's breath of fresh air — between the rich kibbeh sauces, the fierce berbere wats, and the complex injera, this simple salad provides the clean, bright counterpoint that makes the overall meal more complete.
